Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x) = x^2$ and $v(x)=\ln x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={({x}^{2})}^{′}\operatorname{ln}⁡x+{x}^{2}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =2x\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x+{x}^{2}(\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x+x \\  & =x(2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1)\end{aligned}
$$
